sentences.text: Magyarosuchus was a large thalattosuchian, a group of marine crocodylomorphs, possessing a partial jaw that was deeper than those of close relatives like Pelagosaurus.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — preserves many large, recurved teeth with a circular cross-section, non-serrated edges, and vertically aligned grooves.
Fossils include the femur and tibia, measuring 36 cm and 21 cm in length, respectively.
A posterior caudal vertebra in the holotype has a notably larger neural spine, which suggests the presence of a rudimentary vertical tail expansion similar to derived metriorhynchids.
The animal possessed osteoderms arranged in two dorsal rows and at least two ventral rows along its body.
Dorsal osteoderms were mostly square, overlapped the one behind them, and possessed a small lateral ridge.
Ventral osteoderms overlapped front-to-back, were tightly sutured to neighbors, and were much wider than long.
Magyarosuchus is an extinct genus of thalattosuchian first described from fossils found in the Kisgerecse Marl Formation in Hungary.
A fragmentary skeleton of Magyarosuchus was discovered in 1996.
Due to its large size and unique trait combination, Magyarosuchus represents a transitional form between fully marine metriorhynchids and their earlier non-marine ancestors.
Magyarosuchus belongs to the suborder Thalattosuchia.
Magyarosuchus belongs to the superfamily Metriorhynchoidea.
Magyarosuchus is classified as an early member of the clade Metriorhynchoidea.
Magyarosuchus was found in the Kisgerecse Marl Formation, which indicates an open-ocean environment.
Magyarosuchus represents the oldest known thalattosuchian adapted to open-ocean conditions rather than coastal or lagoonal habitats.
The time range for Magyarosuchus is the Toarcian stage, from 180.4 to 174.7 million years ago.
